name: Fascinating History
description: Mind-blowing tales from human history — the Roman Empire, ancient Egypt, World War II, Indian independence, medieval warfare, forgotten civilisations, and the jaw-dropping moments that shaped the world.
style: Cinematic photorealistic, 8K detail, dramatic lighting, period-accurate
example_topics: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid
The Roman concrete that is stronger today than when it was poured 2,000 years ago
The Indian queen who fought the British Empire with her baby strapped to her back
Hitler's stolen art — the 650,000 pieces the Nazis looted across Europe
The Library of Alexandria didn't burn in one night — it died slowly over centuries
Genghis Khan killed so many people he actually cooled the Earth's climate
The 300 Spartans at Thermopylae — what actually happened
voice_style: Intelligent, commanding male narrator with a warm baritone and a storyteller's rhythm. He speaks like a historian who can't help being fascinated — measured authority with moments of quiet intensity when the story demands it. Thinks of Dan Carlin meets David Attenborough.
music_style: {duration} second Epic cinematic orchestral underscore with deep cellos, distant war drums, and sweeping strings. Builds from quiet tension to grand resolution. Period-neutral — works for ancient Rome, medieval Europe, or 20th-century conflict. No vocals, no lyrics.
